title: Commits, Diff & History Inspection
description: Record immutable snapshots with git commit, compare changes with git diff, and navigate history using git log and git show.

blocks.content:
## Recording Snapshots with `git commit`

Once changes are staged, `git commit` captures the state of the index into an immutable commit object:

```bash
git commit -m "feat: add user authentication endpoint"
```

Every commit records:
1. A cryptographic SHA-1/SHA-256 hash identifying the snapshot.
2. A pointer to the root tree object (the project state).
3. Pointers to zero, one, or more parent commits.
4. Author and committer metadata (name, email, timestamp).
5. The commit log message.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C1["Commit: 9b2d1a\nInitial commit"] <-- C2["Commit: f408e2\nfeat: add login"] <-- C3["Commit: 3a91c8 (HEAD -> main)\nfix: validate email"]
```

## Writing Effective Commit Messages

A good commit message explains *why* a change was made, not just *what* changed.

Structure of a conventional commit message:

```
<type>(<scope>): <short summary in imperative mood>

<optional detailed body explaining context and rationale>

<optional footer, e.g. Closes #142>
```

Common commit types:
- `feat`: A new feature for the user.
- `fix`: A bug fix.
- `docs`: Documentation changes only.
- `refactor`: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature.
- `test`: Adding or correcting tests.
- `chore`: Build tasks, package manager configs, etc.

## Inspecting Uncommitted Changes with `git diff`

`git diff` reveals line-level modifications:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    WT["Working Tree"] -->|"git diff"| SA["Staging Area (Index)"]
    SA -->|"git diff --staged / --cached"| HEAD["Last Commit (HEAD)"]
    WT -->|"git diff HEAD"| HEAD
```

- `git diff`: Compares working tree against the staging area (shows unstaged changes).
- `git diff --staged` (or `--cached`): Compares staging area against the last commit (shows what will be committed).
- `git diff HEAD`: Compares working tree directly against the last commit.

## Navigating History with `git log` and `git show`

View the chronological list of commits leading up to the current HEAD:

```bash
# Standard history view
git log

# Compact one-line view with commit hashes
git log --oneline

# Graph view showing branches and merges
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all

# Limit history to the last 3 commits
git log -n 3
```

To view details and patch diff of a specific commit:

```bash
git show 3a91c8
```

blocks.question: Which command displays the exact changes currently staged for the next commit?
blocks.explanation: 'git diff --staged' (or 'git diff --cached') compares changes in the staging index against the HEAD commit.

blocks.question: In Git's commit chain, what does each non-initial commit reference?
options: Its parent commit(s) and a root tree snapshot
A zip archive stored on GitHub
The subsequent child commit in the future
blocks.explanation: Commits in Git form a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Each commit points backward to its parent commit(s) and references a root tree object.
